chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabi' ibn Abdillah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Dissimulation (Taqiyya) is applicable in every necessity, and its performer knows it best when it befalls him.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Dissimulation or concealment of faith to avoid harm
key_terms.صَاحِبُهَا: The one who practices it / its performer

ai.seo_question: What is the scope and authority of Taqiyya in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores that Taqiyya is not merely a passive survival tactic but a dynamic religious duty governed by the individual's discernment of specific circumstances. It highlights the concept of 'personal expertise' in applying dissimulation, distinguishing it from rigid legal formulas, and serves as a foundational text for understanding how early Imams navigated political persecution while maintaining theological integrity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabi’e, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The dissimulation (Taqiyya) (is to be done) during every necessity, and its performer is more knowing with it where he should be indulging in it’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Rib’i from Zurara from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Al-Taqiyyah (protective measures) is for when and wherever needed and the one involved in it knows best how to apply it.”
